findings.description: __aexit__ discards the exception arguments and calls self.__exit__(None, None, None), so any exception raised inside an `async with` attempt block is recorded as a successful result and suppressed instead of being retried.
findings.rationale: Trigger: the body of `async with attempt:` raises an exception (e.g. a network error). The sync __exit__ only records the failure and swallows the exception when exc_type and exc_value are non-None; here they are always None, so it calls set_result(None), marking the attempt successful. The retry loop then stops, and the error is silently dropped, so the caller gets a wrong result rather than a retry or a propagated error.
